claims.evidence: The six Orbitrap .raw files in the file list; PRIDE protocol: "SILAC labelled samples (CHIP WT and CHIP KO each in biological triplicate) ... Orbitrap Elite". The 15 SWATH .wiff runs (TripleTOF 5600+, label-free) and 2 IDA library runs are not SILAC and not annotated.

claims.value: SILAC light = pre-existing proteome; SILAC heavy = newly synthesised proteome (same culture)
claims.evidence: Protocol: "biological triplicates of pulse SILAC samples"; heavy label 13C(6) R and 2H(4) K; "relative peak area of the peptides with the heavy isotope labels with CHIP WT cells/CHIP KO cells ratios". msf Precursor Ions Quantifier QuantificationMethod "SILAC 2 plex (Arg6, Lys4)" in all six files; channel 2 - channel 1 mass deltas 4 / 6 Da (Lys4/Arg6). Median H/(L+H) per run 0.41-0.42 (WT) and 0.36-0.37 (KO), i.e. a partial pulse; heavy is the minority newly made pool. The pulse direction (light pre-grown, heavy pulse) is inferred from "pulse SILAC" + heavy being the quantified readout, not stated verbatim.

CONFLICT recorded: instrument-recorded names are 180327_SP007_CHIP_WT_A, _B, 180328_SP008_CHIP_WT_C_4ul (-> deposited WT_1-3) and 180404_SP007_CHIP_WT_D, _E, _F (-> deposited KO_1-3); all six say "WT", so the string is a series name, not a genotype. Data check: VGF (O15240) has 17/15/20 PSMs in KO_1/2/3 and 0 in WT_1/2/3; in the deposited SWATH t-tests the group with low STUB1 (CHIP KO) has ~10x higher VGF (biorep1 6.30e6 vs 6.43e5, STUB1 4.28e4 vs 1.48e5). So VGF-high = KO, matching the deposited names. Caveat: D-F were also acquired a week later (2018-04-04) than A-C (2018-03-27/28).

limitations: PARTIAL SCOPE (campaign = SILAC): only the 6 pulse-SILAC Orbitrap Elite runs (CHIP_WT_1-3.raw, CHIP_KO_1-3.raw) are annotated. Not annotated because they are label-free: 12 SWATH runs SWATH_SH-SY5Y_SY5Y_CHIP_{WT,KO}_biorep{1,2}_techrep{1,2,3}.wiff (+ .wiff.scan) on the TripleTOF 5600+, and 2 IDA spectral-library runs IDA_SH-SY5Y_SY5Y_CHIP_spectral_library_rep{1,2}.wiff (+ .wiff.scan). They can go in a separate label-free SDRF (rule 12).

No publication describes the SILAC experiment. The iScience 2021 paper (PMC8350547) cites PXD016299 only for the SWATH data and cites "Nita E (2016) MSc thesis, University of Edinburgh" (not retrievable). All SILAC design facts come from the PRIDE protocol, the deposited msf searches and raw headers.

Genotype-to-file identity rests on the deposited file names, while the instrument-recorded names of all six runs read "CHIP_WT_A..F". Supported by the VGF marker (detected only in the deposited KO runs; VGF is ~10x higher in CHIP KO in the deposited SWATH t-tests); STUB1 itself was not detected in any SILAC run. KO runs were acquired one week after the WT runs, so genotype and acquisition batch are confounded.

Pulse direction (light pre-existing, heavy newly synthesised) and pulse duration: the direction is inferred from "pulse SILAC" with heavy as the quantified readout and H/(L+H) < 0.5; the pulse duration is not stated anywhere, so no sampling time is given.
Culture medium (SILAC medium base not named), passage number, reduction/alkylation reagents (FASP, not named), cell type and sample storage temperature are not available.

Search conflict: the PRIDE data processing protocol describes a PD 2.2 Sequest HT search (fragment 0.6 Da, labels static, Met-loss+Acetyl); the deposited msf files are PD 1.4.1.14 Mascot searches (fragment 0.5 Da, SILAC 2plex quant). The SDRF follows the deposited searches.
